start.title: Returning Home
start.text:
You are Jacob. Esau marches with four hundred men.
Your camp waits at the Jabbok ford.

choices.feedback: Genesis 32:13-21 — Jacob prepared a present for Esau, sending droves of animals ahead of him.

choices.text: Attack first — strike before he does
choices.feedback: Bloodshed is not the path. Your hands tremble.

choices.text: Flee back the way you came
choices.feedback: Behind you is Laban. Ahead is the promise.

attack_consequence.title: No Sword for This
attack_consequence.text:
Your sons are few. Esau's men are many.
This is not a battle to win.

choices.feedback: Wisdom replaces fury. You call your servants.

flee_consequence.title: Nowhere to Run
flee_consequence.text:
The road behind is closed. The Lord said: return.
You must face what comes.

choices.text: Turn and prepare gifts for Esau
choices.feedback: You set your face toward your brother again.

send_gifts.title: Droves of Peace
send_gifts.text:
Goats, sheep, camels — sent in waves before you.
"A present for my lord Esau."

choices.text: Pray to the God of your fathers
choices.feedback: Genesis 32:9-12 — Jacob prayed to the God of his father Abraham and his father Isaac, asking for deliverance from Esau.
Pride is a thin shield. Your heart knows it.

boast_consequence.title: The Hollow Boast
boast_consequence.text:
Your words ring empty in the dusk.
You kneel instead, ashamed.

choices.feedback: "Deliver me, I pray, from the hand of my brother."

pray.title: A Prayer at Dusk
pray.text:
"O God of Abraham, of Isaac — save me."
The Jabbok runs cold beside the camp.

choices.text: Send your family across the ford
choices.feedback: Genesis 32:22-23 — Jacob sent his wives, his two female servants, and his eleven children across the Jabbok ford.
Your soul needs the night alone. You know it.

stay_consequence.title: Crowded Hearts
stay_consequence.text:
Voices, children, bleating animals.
This night calls for silence.

choices.feedback: You wave them on. The water swallows their footsteps.

send_family.title: All Across the Jabbok
send_family.text:
The last torch fades on the far bank.
You stand alone. The river hushes.

choices.text: Stay on this side — face the night
choices.feedback: Genesis 32:24 — Jacob was left alone on his side of the Jabbok.

choices.text: Cross over to your family now
choices.feedback: Something holds you back. The night is not finished.

cross_consequence.title: Drawn Back
cross_consequence.text:
You step into the water and stop.
A presence waits behind you.

choices.text: Return to the bank — stay alone
choices.feedback: You climb back. The river quiets again.

alone.title: Jacob Was Left Alone
alone.text:
Footsteps. A figure in the dark.
A man stands before you — silent, strong.

choices.feedback: Genesis 32:24 — A man wrestled with Jacob until daybreak.

choices.text: Run from him into the night
choices.feedback: He is faster. You cannot escape this.

choices.text: Beg him to leave you in peace
choices.feedback: He does not answer. He waits for you.

run_consequence.title: He Is Always There
run_consequence.text:
However far you turn, he is before you.
This fight cannot be avoided.

choices.feedback: You raise your arms. The night begins.

beg_consequence.title: Silence in Reply
beg_consequence.text:
He will not let you pass without struggle.
This is your night to wrestle.

choices.feedback: Your hands close on his robe. The wrestling starts.

the_struggle.title: All Through the Night
the_struggle.text:
You wrestle. Hours pass. Neither yields.
Your breath burns. He does not tire.

choices.text: Hold on — do not let go
choices.feedback: Genesis 32:26 — The man told Jacob, "Let me go, for it is daybreak," but Jacob replied, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."

choices.text: Give up — he is too strong
choices.feedback: Something deeper in you refuses. You grip again.

give_up_consequence.title: Not Yet
give_up_consequence.text:
Your knees buckle, but your hands will not open.
This night must be finished.

choices.feedback: You rise once more, and the struggle goes on.

the_touch.title: A Touch at the Hip
the_touch.text:
He reaches out — your hip turns out of joint.
Pain blooms. Yet you do not release him.

choices.feedback: Genesis 32:26 — Jacob said, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."
Bitterness will not bless you. Reach again.

curse_consequence.title: Words That Wound You
curse_consequence.text:
Your curses fall like stones in the river.
But his hand is still within reach.

choices.text: Cling to him — ask for blessing
choices.feedback: You grasp his robe. "Bless me — I will not let go."

demand_blessing.title: The Question
demand_blessing.text:
He says: "What is your name?"
The river holds its breath.

choices.feedback: Genesis 32:27 — Jacob answered, "Jacob."
Deceit will not free you here. Speak truth.
He sees through you. The name must come.

hide_name_consequence.title: He Knows Already
hide_name_consequence.text:
His gaze does not leave you.
You cannot lie to such eyes.

choices.feedback: The word breaks loose like a stone from your chest.

boast_name_consequence.title: No Crown Will Do
boast_name_consequence.text:
Titles fall away in this place.
Only your true name remains.

choices.feedback: You bow your head. The name is laid down.

new_name.title: Israel
new_name.text:
"No longer Jacob — but Israel.
For you have struggled with God and prevailed."

choices.feedback: Genesis 32:28 — The angel renamed Jacob to Israel because he had struggled with God and with humans and had overcome.

choices.text: Refuse — you do not deserve it
choices.feedback: He gives. You do not earn. Receive.

refuse_consequence.title: It Is Given
refuse_consequence.text:
The name is not yours to refuse.
It is His gift, freely given.

choices.feedback: You whisper: "Israel." The river answers softly.

name_him.title: Tell Me Your Name
name_him.text:
You ask: "Tell me your name."
He answers only: "Why do you ask?"

choices.feedback: Genesis 32:29 — The angel did not reveal his name to Jacob, but instead blessed him there.
Some names are not for men. Be still.

demand_name_consequence.title: Holy Silence
demand_name_consequence.text:
He will not speak it.
The blessing is what he gives.

choices.feedback: You bow. His hand rests upon your head.

blessing.title: He Blessed Him There
blessing.text:
The first light touches the eastern hills.
His blessing flows through you.

choices.feedback: Genesis 32:30 — Jacob named the place Peniel, saying that he had seen God face to face and yet his life was spared.
Such mercy must be remembered, not buried.

secret_consequence.title: It Must Be Marked
secret_consequence.text:
Hidden grace fades from memory.
This place must bear the witness.

choices.feedback: You set the name upon the ground. Peniel.

peniel.title: Peniel — The Face of God
peniel.text:
The sun rises over Peniel.
You rise too — and limp upon your hip.

choices.text: Cross the Jabbok to meet Esau
choices.feedback: You walk forward, marked, blessed, no longer the same.

to_esau.title: Israel Goes Forward
to_esau.text:
The river is behind you. Esau waits ahead.
You are Israel. The journey continues.
